A Berkeley study estimated restaurant price pass-through from higher wages at about 60% to 70%, implying a 10% labor-cost increase is associated with roughly a 6% to 7% menu-price increase.

A Chicago Fed study found that during months with a minimum-wage hike, the mean price change in limited-service outlets more than doubled to 0.88%, and implied prices in limited-service restaurants rose 1.56% on average in response to a 10% minimum-wage increase.

The National Restaurant Association says most restaurants operate on pre-tax profit margins of 3-5%, and its inflation infographic estimates an average price increase of 26.2% is needed to cover higher input costs and maintain margin.

A 2026 NBER study found food-away-from-home prices in California’s four in-sample MSAs increased 3.3% to 3.6% relative to 17 control MSAs through December 2024, consistent with cost pass-through rather than pure margin expansion.
